reason: Verified in source and by driving master.html?v=approach at 1440. (1) .b-grab has no click handler anywhere in render-b.js; clicking it leaves .b-field byte-identical, while its own accessible name promises 'Open to change it' - a control that says it is a door and is not. (2) The .b-seg buttons (render-b.js ~line 257) are rendered with static aria-pressed true/false and no handler; after clicking 'Kept private' the pair still reads ['On the plan=true','Kept private=false'] and the row chip still reads 'shown' with the label 'Shown to guests'. On the highest-stakes decision in the product - what the guests can see - the surface gives no evidence a choice was made. (3) .b-measure carries role='list' with 7 .b-item children and 0 [role='listitem'] descendants (both owner-flight and owner-editing): a screen reader announces a list of nothing and all seven rows fall outside it. Neither gate covers any of this - interaction-check.mjs only reads .b-grab aria-labels, audit.mjs has no list-semantics or aria-pressed assertion. The one overstatement: the chip is a real button, so it does get cursor:pointer from shell.css:200 and a hover ground (.b-grab:hover -> var(--fore-06)); it is the row (.b-item: background rgba(0,0,0,0), cursor auto, no :hover and no :focus-within rule) that has no state at all. That does not save the finding - a 54x28 uppercase mono chip at 62% ink reading SHOWN is a status badge before it is a door, and the hover only exists once the pointer is already on it. The fix stays inside the palette (var(--fore-04) exists, shell.css:81/94), adds no weight and no family.
